AI assistant skill

Source: vignettes/articles/rbest-assistant.Rmd
rbest-assistant.Rmd

RBesT comes with an agent skill, rbest-assistant, that helps AI assistants guide RBesT workflows: MAP priors from historical controls, robustification, ESS, decision rules, operating characteristics and probability of success. It asks before it codes and only uses verified, runnable snippets.

Please read before use. The RBesT functions are tested and validated; the AI agent’s output is not. The skill only guides the agent: which code it writes, which inputs and assumptions it uses, and how it interprets the results is decided by the agent alone. It is not controlled by RBesT, it can differ between runs of the same prompt, and it may be wrong. Treat it like a draft from a colleague: check the code, the inputs and the conclusions, and rely only on results you have reproduced by running the code yourself. Any analysis or design must be reviewed by a qualified statistician. The assistant is experimental and may change; watch for updates, and send us your feedback via GitHub issues.

Getting started

Once the skill is installed (see below), try:

Using the RBesT assistant skill: give me a short introduction to MAP priors. How can I use historical control data for a new trial? No analysis yet, just an overview. Then briefly tell me what else you can help me with in RBesT.

Naming the skill in plain words works with every assistant and install type. To invoke it directly instead, type /rbest:rbest-assistant if you installed the plugin (Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Posit Assistant, VS Code), or /rbest-assistant if you installed the skill on its own (in Codex: $rbest-assistant).

Installation

Most routes install the skill straight from the GitHub repository; no package release is needed:

  • Claude Cowork: Customize → Plugins → Add marketplace → Novartis/RBesT, then install rbest.
  • Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add Novartis/RBesT, then /plugin install rbest@rbest.
  • Claude Desktop and other apps that install skills by upload: download rbest-assistant.zip from the latest GitHub release and upload it as a skill (in Claude Desktop under Customize → Skills). Use this route if you cannot add a plugin marketplace. The zip holds the skill of that release, which can be older than the copy in the repository that the other routes install. Releases from RBesT 1.12-1 on have the zip attached.
  • ChatGPT Codex (CLI, IDE extension or app): Codex reads skills from ~/.agents/skills (for you) or .agents/skills (for one project). Run npx skills add Novartis/RBesT, use the R snippet under “Without plugins” below, or ask Codex’s built-in $skill-installer to install inst/skills/rbest-assistant from the Novartis/RBesT GitHub repository. Invoke it with $rbest-assistant.
  • Other agents: npx skills add Novartis/RBesT (skill only).

Each installed version of RBesT also bundles a copy of the skill that matches it, at system.file("skills/rbest-assistant", package = "RBesT").

Any other tool: ask it to install the skill. The skill uses the open Agent Skills format: a folder named rbest-assistant that contains a SKILL.md file (YAML frontmatter with name and description, then Markdown instructions) and a references/ folder of Markdown files. Most AI assistants that support skills read this format. Paste this prompt into yours:

Help me install the rbest-assistant agent skill. It is in the open Agent Skills format: a folder rbest-assistant containing SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter with name and description) and a references/ folder. Its source is the GitHub repository Novartis/RBesT, folder inst/skills/rbest-assistant; it is also part of the installed RBesT R package at system.file("skills/rbest-assistant", package = "RBesT"). The repository root is also a Claude-format plugin marketplace (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json, plugin rbest). Tell me which install route you support (plugin, skill folder, or installer command), where you look for skills, walk me through installing it, and show me how to check that the skill is loaded. Keep the folder name rbest-assistant, since it must match the name in SKILL.md.

Updating

  • Claude Code: /plugin marketplace update rbest, or turn on auto-update for the marketplace under /plugin → Marketplaces.
  • Claude Cowork, Posit Assistant and VS Code: use the update action of the app’s plugin settings (details below for Posit Assistant and VS Code).
  • Skill-only installs (npx skills, Codex, a copied folder, an uploaded zip): repeat the install; for the zip, download it again from the latest release and replace the uploaded skill. The copy bundled with RBesT updates with the package.

Positron, RStudio and VS Code

  • Positron / RStudio with Posit Assistant (recommended). Posit Assistant reads the Claude marketplace format. Open ⋯ → Plugins (or /plugin) → Marketplaces, add Novartis/RBesT, then install rbest from Browse. You do not need rbest-r, because Posit Assistant runs R itself. To update, use “Check for updates” on the marketplace, then Update. The skill appears as /rbest:rbest-assistant. See the Posit Assistant plugin docs.

  • VS Code. VS Code agent plugins read the Claude plugin and marketplace format. Add Novartis/RBesT as a marketplace (Chat: Open Customizations → Browse → Configure Marketplaces), or use the install links for rbest and rbest-r (deep link: vscode://chat-plugin/install?source=Novartis%2FRBesT&plugin=rbest, or plugin=rbest-r). This needs the chat.plugins.enabled setting. Updates come through “Check for and Apply Updates”. Enterprise Copilot policy may restrict marketplaces or MCP servers.

  • Without plugins, in either editor, copy the skill bundled with your installed RBesT version:

    dir.create("~/.agents/skills", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
file.copy(system.file("skills/rbest-assistant", package = "RBesT"),
          "~/.agents/skills", recursive = TRUE)

    or run npx skills add Novartis/RBesT.

  • R connector without the plugin: see btw’s MCP documentation for the .vscode/mcp.json or user mcp.json entry that runs btw::btw_mcp_server().

Running the code

Results come from RBesT only. The skill instructs the agent to compute exclusively with the RBesT package in an R session, and never to re-create its functionality in another language or with its own code. What the agent delivers therefore depends on whether it can reach an R with RBesT:

  • It can: it runs the analysis there and reports the results together with the code.
  • It cannot: it says so and offers either to guide you through the setup (R, RBesT, and a way for the agent to use them), or to write one self-contained R script that you download and run yourself. In that case it reports no results; you can bring the output back to have it interpreted.

If your organisation does not allow an agent to run R for you, or requires analyses to run on a dedicated computing platform, tell the agent. It then works in script-only mode from the start.

The skill names the few cases in which the agent may add numerical code of its own in R on top of RBesT. At present there is one: assurance for a design prior that links the two arms, which pos2S() cannot express. It is obtained by quasi-Monte Carlo averaging of oc2S() results (using a QMC package such as spacefillr) and is always reported with its Monte Carlo standard error. Should an agent present results that it computed in any other way, discard them and please let us know.

Recommended ways to have the code actually run: Posit Assistant in Positron or RStudio runs R in your live session, so it needs no connector. Coding agents such as Claude Code or Copilot agent mode can call Rscript themselves.

Optional rbest-r connector. This is mainly for Claude Cowork and Claude Desktop, whose sandbox cannot reach your R. The rbest-r plugin from the same marketplace starts btw’s MCP server so that the agent can run R code in your local R installation. It needs a local R with RBesT, btw and ideally ragg, and works on macOS and Linux. Install RBesT as a ready-built binary rather than from source, preferably from Posit Public Package Manager, which also serves Linux binaries; the agent can guide you through it. It runs R code without a sandbox; the app asks before each call. Organisations may disable local MCP servers; the skill still works then, and the agent hands over an R script instead. To get help with setup, ask your agent:

Help me set up the optional rbest-r plugin from the Novartis/RBesT marketplace so my AI agent can run R code via the btw MCP server. I’m on [macOS/Windows/Linux]. Walk me through installing what’s needed, checking that the connector starts, and fixing it if Rscript isn’t found.

For Windows and manual setups, see btw’s MCP documentation.
